To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis and preliminary evaluation are reported of a doxorycin-formaldehyde conjugates tethered to the antiandrogen, cyano-nilutamide, for treatment of prostate cancer, and the relative ability of the tether to bind to the androgen receptors was studied as a funciton of tether.

a tethered cyanonilutamidyl doxorubicin conjugate has a relative binding of 10% for human androgen binding domain and that the tethered cyanoniltamide doxorubicin-conjugate has the same in vitro cytotoxicity as the free doxorubicin in a PC-3 prostate cancer cell line.

we have developed an antiandrogen-based targeted cytotoxin for the treatment of hormone-dependent prostate cancer and we have shown that a butynediol tether is an effective linker between the antiandrogen and the cytotoxin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a targeted drug for the treatment of hormone-refractory prostate cancer.
the development of a targeted cytotoxin that is designed to bind specifically to androgen receptor.
the development of a new class of targeted drugs for the treatment of androgen receptor-dependent tumors such as prostate cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the tethering group has a profound effect on the relative binding affinity of the tethered cyanonilutamides to the androgen receptors, and that the tethering groups that have been explored in this study are not optimal for this purpose.
the linear region of a tether between a targeting group and a cytotoxin is not a major determinant of the relative affinity for the human androgen-receptor.
the tethered antiandrogen-drug conjugate is a promising candidate for further evaluation in a tumor model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the linear region of a tether connecting the targeting group to a cytotoxin can be designed to have a binding affinity to the androgen binding site that is sufficient for the targeted drug to bind to the androgen receptors on prostate cancer cells.
we have demonstrated that the tethering of a doxorubin-formaldehyde derivative to an antiandrogen is feasible.
a tether of the butynedioloxy-ethylenoxy-ethylenoxy-type is a reasonable tether to use in a targeted drug for androgen receptor-mediated delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tether can be designed to have sufficient flexibility for binding to the human androgene receptor and to allow the release of the cytotoxin from the targeting moiety.
the design of an androgen receptor-targeting group tethered to a cytotoxin is not a trivial task.
the tether connecting the cytotoxin to the antiandrogen can be as short as 3 carbon atoms and still retain a relative binding affinity that is 10% of nilutamides binding.
